uncited: Early Termination and Probabilistic Path Control are acceleration techniques that reduce the computational cost of volume rendering by halting the ray-marching integration loop when the remaining contribution to the pixel is deemed negligible.

Unlike [Occlusion Clipping with Orthogonal Opacity Map](990-occlusion-clipping-with-orthogonal-opacity-map.md) which culls based on pre-computed opacity maps, or [Empty-space skipping](1002-empty-space-skipping.md) which skips geometrically empty regions, these methods operate on the accumulated state of the ray during traversal.

They set themselves apart from [Bounding Volume Culling](1239-bounding-volume-culling.md) by relying on optical properties (opacity/transmittance) rather than geometric bounds, and from [Adaptive Multi-Step Empty Voxel Skipping](6289-adaptive-multi-step-empty-voxel-skipping.md) by focusing on the termination of the integration path rather than the step size.
**Culling/Skipping:** Identifying regions of the volume or ray path that do not contribute to the final image (e.g., empty space, occluded voxels) and bypassing their evaluation .
by introducing conditions that break the loop early, skip iterations, or reduce the number of $C_{sample}$ queries.
During inferencing, points exit only once at a specific stage.
Points found earlier to be reliable immediately exit and are rendered.
Which branch is taken depends on clustering results.
The concept of early termination in volume rendering has evolved from simple opacity thresholds to sophisticated probabilistic and uncertainty-aware methods.
